_README: REVIEW-TRIGGER list, not a permission list -- same rule as DEFAULT_WATCHLIST
in trust_runtime.py: a match here never grants access by itself.
Legal basis is TRADEMARK (brand/company names, and in some cases
registered product-line names), NOT the Epic IP Partner Licensing
Agreement channel that license_manifest.json documents for LEGO/TMNT/
Star Wars/etc. There is no known Epic-brokered UEFN license pathway for
any of these lab/analytical-equipment manufacturers as of 2026-08-02.
That means: matching a term here should resolve to BLOCKED unless your
studio has a REAL, independently-negotiated document from that specific
rightsholder (license_type='creator_independent_license' in
license_manifest.json) -- e.g. a genuine sponsored-training-sim deal
with a real manufacturer for an educational/onboarding build. Never add
a manifest entry for one of these terms because a partnership 'seems
plausible' -- that is exactly the fabricated-relationship failure mode
trust_runtime.py's module docstring warns against.
KNOWN FALSE-POSITIVE RISK: entries flagged
'false_positive_risk': 'high' use a short or generic-sounding brand
name (e.g. IKA, Roche) that can appear as a substring of unrelated
words once normalized (letters/digits only, per
TrustRuntime._normalize). Before enabling this file in production,
review those entries and prefer a qualifying alias
('ika-werke', 'roche diagnostics') over the bare short form if false
positives show up in your own audit log.
SCOPE LIMIT: this is a text-match gate over tool-call payloads (asset
names, prompts, labels, code strings). It cannot detect a 3D model that
visually replicates a real instrument's industrial design without ever
naming the brand in text -- that is a separate, unsolved problem this
file does not claim to cover.
English-only: this file (and every other file in this repo)
intentionally carries no non-English terms. An earlier revision added
transliterated aliases for several high-likelihood entries (Thermo
Fisher, Agilent, Illumina, Roche Diagnostics, Eppendorf, Sartorius,
Shimadzu, Bruker) to catch non-English-language references to the
same brands; those aliases were removed by policy, so that coverage
gap is open again.
Sourced from the manufacturer list supplied 2026-08-02 (broad-line,
general-lab, analytical/spectrometric, and biotech-equipment vendors).
Sub-brands owned by a parent company are listed as their own terms
because prompts/asset names are more likely to reference the sub-brand
than the parent (e.g. 'Invitrogen' rather than 'Thermo Fisher').

leica microsystems.notes: Distinct legal entity from Leica Camera AG (unrelated company, cameras) -- do not conflate when documenting a manifest entry.

milliporesigma.notes: MilliporeSigma is the U.S./Canada life-science brand of Merck KGaA (which trades as EMD in North America for trademark reasons unrelated to Merck & Co., Inc. -- two separate companies).

ika.notes: Three-letter brand name -- prefer the 'ika-werke' alias in production watchlists to reduce substring false positives from unrelated normalized text.

waters corporation.notes: 'Waters' alone is too generic (common English word) -- only the qualified forms are listed as terms/aliases on purpose.

perkinelmer.notes: Company renamed part of its business to Revvity in 2023 -- if generating current-day content, verify which entity name is live before writing a manifest entry.

roche diagnostics.notes: 'Roche' alone is a common surname -- only the qualified 'roche diagnostics' form is listed as a term on purpose.
